record.context_brief: Topological full groups of Polish-group actions
record.original_question: For the topological full groups arising from continuous actions of Polish groups on compact Polish spaces, especially actions of the real line, what general structure results hold? In particular, when are these groups coarsely bounded, when do they admit a dense finitely generated subgroup, how many such groups are there, and can one classify their actions by homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: More generally, one can use the approach from [8] to show that given a Polish group G acting continuously on a compact Polish space X, one can associate to it a Polish group, the topological full group of the action.

Question 4.6. What can we say about these topological full groups, especially when the acting group is the real line? For instance, when are they coarsely bounded in the sense of [37]? When do they admit a dense finitely generated group? How many such groups are there? Can one classify their actions by homeomorphisms?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a Polish group (a topological group whose underlying space is separable and completely metrizable) acting continuously on a compact Polish space $X$. Define the topological full group of this action to be the group of all homeomorphisms $h \colon X \to X$ for which there exists an open cover $X = U_1 \cup \cdots \cup U_n$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $h(x) = g_i \cdot x$ for every $x \in U_i$ and every $i$; equip this group with its natural Polish group topology.

Recall that a subset $A$ of a topological group $H$ is coarsely bounded (in the sense of Rosendal) if $A$ has finite diameter with respect to every continuous left-invariant pseudometric on $H$, equivalently, if every continuous isometric action of $H$ on a metric space has bounded $A$-orbits. The group $H$ itself is called coarsely bounded if $H$ is a coarsely bounded subset of itself.

Investigate the structure of the topological full groups arising in this way, with special emphasis on the case $G = \mathbb{R}$:

1. Characterize when such a topological full group is coarsely bounded.
2. Characterize when such a topological full group admits a dense finitely generated subgroup.
3. Determine, up to isomorphism, how many topological full groups arise in this manner.
4. Provide a classification of the continuous actions by homeomorphisms of such topological full groups on compact Polish spaces.

artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this cluster of questions about topological full groups associated to continuous Polish-group actions on compact Polish spaces was found. The framework of coarse boundedness (Rosendal) and topological full groups is actively studied, but no source addressing precisely these structural questions for actions of the real line was located. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Coarse Geometry of Topological Groups — Rosendal
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces coarse boundedness for Polish groups as a replacement for compactness.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework for the coarse boundedness notion referenced, but does not resolve the questions for topological full groups of Polish-group actions.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey of techniques for Polish groups and full groups.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys related techniques without resolving the listed questions about topological full groups of Polish-group actions.
